meta_title: CacheTrace · Cache memory simulator with Excel export
meta_desc: Simulate cache memory instruction by instruction: direct-mapped, 2-way and 4-way set-associative, and fully associative. Address bit split, hits, misses, evictions and Excel export. Free and open source.
lead: Work out hits, misses and evictions instruction by instruction in direct-mapped, 2-way and 4-way set-associative, and fully associative caches. Export the tables to Excel.
hero_meta: Browser · No installation · MIT license · Open source
stat1: cache organizations for the same program
stat2: servers: everything is computed in your browser
stat3: accesses of the sample exercise, solved instantly
f_title: The whole exercise, access by access.
f_sub: From the problem statement to the direct-mapped, SA2W, SA4W and FA tables, without redoing the maths by hand.
c1_p: The same program is replayed on direct-mapped, 2-way, 4-way and fully associative caches, with a comparison of hits and evictions.
c2_p: Every address is split into tag, index and offset with fixed colours, derived from the address bus, the cache size and the bytes per line.
c3_p: Every instruction produces a Fetch; lw and sw add their data access. Step through the program and inspect the cache and registers after each instruction.
c4_p: RISC-style instructions (li, lw, lb, sb, addi, bne…) with byte, half-word and word accesses, labels or address jumps, the zero register and byte-by-byte memory dumps.
c5_p: Write-back with write-allocate, LRU or FIFO, and invalid lines taken in order. The conventions are documented and covered by tests.
c6_p: A workbook with one sheet per cache, formulas for the bits, the final state, the evolution of the accesses and the register history.
x_title: An Excel with formulas, not screenshots.
x1: One sheet per organization: DM, SA2W, SA4W and FA, whichever you choose
x2: Tag, index and offset bits computed with formulas from the address
x3: Final cache state with bytes D0–D7 and instructions shown as I_n
x4: Evolution sheets for the cache and the registers after every instruction
x5: A Statement sheet with the parameters, the program and the dump
x_note: The .xlsx workbooks open in Excel and LibreOffice. Evolution sheets are optional.
w_title: From the statement to the table in three steps.
s1_p: Address bus, cache size and bytes per line; then the program and the memory dump.
s2_p: A functional processor runs the program and every access is replayed on the four caches.
s3_p: Step through the result instruction by instruction and download the Excel with the caches you need.
m_sub: CacheTrace always applies the same rules and documents them, so you can check the result against your own problem statement.
m2: invalid lines are filled in order
p1_c: The app interface is currently in Spanish
p1_d: .xlsx workbooks open in Excel and LibreOffice
p2_p: CacheTrace is a study tool. It models a unified cache with a fixed write policy; it does not replace a hardware simulator or the official solution to your course. Always check the results against your own problem statement.
fin_sub: No sign-up, MIT license. Try the sample exercise or load your own.
foot_desc: Cache memory simulator for computer architecture exercises.
foot_made: What you enter is processed in your browser
